entries.postTitle: How to Stop Drifting

captions.threads:
1/4 You had a plan six months ago. Something concrete. A project, a move, a version of yourself that actually knew what the next three months looked like. Now you're here and you can't quite remember what you were thinking, which is weird because it wasn't that long ago.

2/4 The drift doesn't announce itself. It's not like you woke up one day and chose confusion. It's tiny decisions that felt fine in the moment. Saying yes to something shiny. Pivoting because the original thing got harder. Listening to everyone's opinions about what you should do instead. You're not lost exactly. You're just not following the map anymore.

3/4 Here's what actually happens to people like us: we need the friction of specificity more than we think. The wandering feels like freedom until it becomes a fog you can't navigate. We convince ourselves that having options means we're doing better, when really we're just experiencing option paralysis in real time.

4/4 The reframe isn't about finding your one true north. It's smaller than that. You don't drift because you're broken. You drift because part of you is still hungry for something clearer, and that hunger is the actual signal. The plan doesn't have to be perfect. It just has to be chosen. https://vibrationofawesome.com/blog/boom/posts/how-to-stop-drifting

entries.postTitle: Seeing the Gap: How to Notice When Your Life Doesn't Fit Anymore

captions.threads:
The gap between your life and your actual self grows quietly. You don't notice it at first because nothing is technically broken. Bills paid. People still love you. Coffee still tastes like coffee.

1/4 But there's a hum underneath everything now. A frequency that doesn't match. You catch yourself in the mirror and barely recognize the person looking back. Not because you've aged or changed physically. Because somewhere along the way you stopped believing in what you're building.

2/4 I used to think this meant I was broken. Ungrateful even. Turns out I was just outgrowing a life that never fit in the first place. The gap isn't a sign of failure. It's the universe getting louder. Your soul finally screaming loud enough that even your logical brain has to listen.

3/4 Here's what most people miss: noticing the gap is actually the easy part. Living inside it while you rebuild? That requires a different kind of courage. Not the motivation-poster kind. The messy, uncertain, fully human kind where you don't know the ending but you move anyway.

4/4 Stop waiting for permission to feel wrong about something that isn't working. Your discomfort is data. It's your internal compass pointing toward what's actually true for you.

If this lands, let it change how you move today.

entries.postTitle: How Overstimulation Affects Focus

captions.threads:
Your nervous system doesn't care how important that email is. When you're overstimulated, comprehension just stops working. Your eyes move. Words land nowhere. You're reading the same sentence four times like you've never seen language before.

1/4 This isn't a focus problem. This is a regulation problem. There's a difference and it matters because it changes what actually fixes it. You can't willpower your way out of overstimulation. Your nervous system doesn't have a willpower setting.

2/4 I spent years thinking I was lazy or broken. Turns out I was just constantly firing on too many cylinders. Too much input, too many tabs, too many notifications, too much context switching. The bandwidth was already maxed before I tried to read anything serious.
